facts.t: The Constitution gives the Governor no fixed term
facts.d: Article 156 says the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President. The five-year figure in the same article is expressly subject to that pleasure — which is why B. P. Singhal had to hold that removal still cannot be arbitrary.

facts.t: The Supreme Court set assent deadlines, then unset them
facts.d: In April 2025 the Court fixed timelines under Article 200 — one month to assent, three months to reserve, and for the first time a three-month limit on the President. Later that year, answering a Presidential Reference, it reversed those timelines.

facts.t: Article 175 dropped four words from the 1935 Act
facts.d: Its colonial predecessor let the Governor send messages to the legislature in his discretion. The Constitution deleted that phrase — the omission Nabam Rebia relied on to hold that the Governor is not the conscience keeper of the Assembly.

o: For a fixed term of five years
During the pleasure of the President
During the pleasure of the Chief Minister
Until removed by the state legislature
bank.e: Article 156(1). The five-year reference is subject to that pleasure, which is why the office has no security of tenure.

bank.q: With reference to the Governor's address to the legislature, consider the following statements:
s: Article 176 uses the word shall, making the special address a constitutional duty.
Article 163 binds the Governor to aid and advice except where discretion is expressly conferred.
The Governor may edit the cabinet-approved text before delivering it.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Governor is a constitutional reader, not an editor — omitting portions distorts responsible government.

bank.q: Match List I (committee or case) with List II (recommendation or holding on the Governor):
pairs: 1. Removal cannot be arbitrary and needs valid, compelling reasons
2. An eminent outsider detached from politics, appointed after consulting the Chief Minister
3. The Governor is not the Centre's agent
4. Fixed tenure and transparent panel-based selection
bank.e: Sarkaria proposed the eminent-outsider convention, Punchhi fixed tenure and panel selection, B. P. Singhal constrained removal, and Rajamannar insisted the Governor is not the Centre's agent.

bank.q: Arrange the Sarkaria–Punchhi order of invitation for government formation:
items: Post-electoral coalition with all partners in government
The largest single party with support
bank.e: Pre-poll alliance first, then the largest single party able to demonstrate support, then a post-electoral coalition with all partners in government, and finally an alliance relying on outside support.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about a hung assembly?
o: The floor test is decisive, not arithmetic at Raj Bhavan
A Governor may demand signed letters of an absolute majority before administering the oath
A Governor may seek support letters as prima facie evidence
Majority is ordinarily to be proved within thirty days
bank.e: The Governor cannot insist on proof of absolute majority before the oath — minority governments are constitutionally possible, and Article 189 decides questions by a majority of those present and voting.

bank.as: The Governor's discretion in a hung assembly is a temporary mechanism, not a personal preference.
bank.rs: S. R. Bommai held that the Assembly, not the Raj Bhavan, determines who commands a majority.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Subhash Desai (2023) added that even the discretion to call a floor test is not unfettered.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the 2025 assent timelines:
s: The Supreme Court prescribed one month to grant or withhold assent.
It prescribed three months where a Bill is reserved for the President.
It also, for the first time, set a time limit for the President to decide on referred Bills.
bank.e: All three were part of the April 2025 ruling — which the Court subsequently reversed while answering a Presidential Reference.

bank.q: Which case established that the President and Governor act on ministerial advice outside expressly specified discretionary areas?
o: Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab
bank.e: Shamsher Singh. Nabam Rebia dealt specifically with messages to the House under Article 175.

bank.q: All of the following are arguments for retaining the office of Governor EXCEPT:
o: It provides a constitutional check upholding the federal structure
It offers stability during hung assemblies and constitutional breakdowns
It serves as a Centre–State communication channel
It allows the Union to review state legislation on policy merits
bank.e: That is the criticism, not the justification. Every expert body — Rajamannar, Sarkaria, Punchhi — recommends reform of the office rather than its use as an instrument of central policy review.

bank.q: The minimum age qualification for appointment as Governor under Article 157 is:
bank.e: Thirty-five years, alongside Indian citizenship. The minimal criteria — with no bar on active politicians — is itself a standard criticism.

bank.q: With reference to Rameshwar Prasad (2006), consider the following statements:
s: It held that dissolving a freshly elected assembly on the apprehension of horse-trading is unconstitutional.
It reinforced that the floor test, not conjecture, settles the question of majority.
It abolished the Governor's discretion under Article 164.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The discretion under Article 164 survives — what the case constrained was its pre-emptive, speculative exercise.
